decisive_items: his lips were markedly edematous, with multiple superficial ulcers having heaped‐up margins
progressive lip swelling with painful ulcerations
Gram stain, acid-fast stain, and mucicarmine stain of lesion samples were negative
response.rationale: Kaposi's sarcoma is the specific HIV-associated mucocutaneous diagnosis that best fits ulcerated, heaped-up lip lesions after infectious and complement-mediated causes are excluded; R1 explains the immune-reconstitution timing but is less specific.

rejected.why: Negative fungal stains, cultures, and Histoplasma antigen tests exclude fungal infection.
Normal C1 esterase inhibitor levels and painful ulcerations argue strongly against angioedema.
HSV PCR from the ulcer base was negative.
Lack of response to antibiotics and absence of supportive Bartonella evidence make bacillary angiomatosis unlikely.
